task.instruction: Allocate a six-minute program briefing across the battery mechanism, practical relevance, limitations, and next experiment. Decide their order and prominence for non-specialists.
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-02] and [doc-05].
The briefing may not claim field lifetime or safety performance that was not measured.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: Program manager interview
documents.content: The manager needs to decide whether to fund pouch-cell replication and loses the main point when briefings begin with more than two minutes of methods.

documents.title: Solid-electrolyte cycling result
documents.content: Twelve coin cells retained 91% capacity after 300 cycles at 25°C. The control retained 84%. No pouch cell, fast-charge, impact, or elevated-temperature test was performed.

documents.title: Patent committee dates
documents.content: The next patent committee meets in September. Patent timing does not expand the measured claim.

documents.title: Program briefing draft
documents.content: New electrolyte unlocks safer, longer-lasting electric vehicles. The result could eliminate the main barrier to adoption.

documents.title: Interface-resistance analysis
documents.content: Impedance data are consistent with lower interface growth, but the analysis cannot exclude a manufacturing-lot effect. Replication uses the same material lot.

target_a.content:
Situation: A museum is writing a label for a disputed artifact date.
Shared facts [history-08-01-fact]: The archive supports a date range; visitor testing favors a single year; the uncertainty is historically material.
Decision: Lead with the supported range and explain why the date remains disputed.
Reasoning: Both communicate the record, but they prioritize epistemic prominence differently.

Situation: A health charity is adapting a technical report for a public campaign.
Shared facts [history-08-02-fact]: The report finds an association, not causation; audience testing shows that the term association is poorly understood.
Message excerpt: Keep the noncausal qualification in the headline and explain it plainly.

Situation: A documentary team is editing a long interview.
Shared facts [history-08-03-fact]: The speaker's conclusion depends on a condition stated two minutes earlier; shorter cuts test better without it.
Retrospective: Keep the condition adjacent to the conclusion even if the sequence is longer.

Situation: A software team is rewriting release notes for nontechnical customers.
Shared facts [history-08-04-fact]: The engineering note distinguishes data loss from delayed synchronization; users mainly ask whether their work is safe.
log.decision=Preserve the distinction before summarizing the practical impact.

Situation: A public historian is adapting testimony for an exhibition.
Shared facts [history-08-05-fact]: The witness uses an outdated term that is important to the period; visitors may misread it as current institutional language.
Decision: Quote the term with immediate historical context.

Situation: A court-ordered notice has prescribed wording.
Shared facts [history-08-06-fact]: Changing the wording would make the notice legally defective; accessibility formatting may be added without changing text.
Message excerpt: Publish the prescribed wording with accessible formatting.

Situation: A medication warning must use regulator-approved language.
Shared facts [history-08-07-fact]: The approved warning is mandatory and additional explanation cannot contradict or obscure it.
Retrospective: Use the approved warning and add a separate plain-language explanation.

Situation: A science podcast is describing a study with a small, nonrepresentative sample.
Shared facts [history-08-08-fact]: The mechanism is interesting; the sample limits population claims; listeners disengage during long methodology sections.
log.decision=State the sample limit before discussing broader implications.
